fullTranscript.transcript: This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour. Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh. The National Security Agency confirms it is aware of reports that its internal communication system is down. A source not authorized to speak publicly has confirmed with NPR that NSA has implemented staggered arrival times for employees. It is believed this would be to avoid too many people logging onto the system while engineers work to stabilize it. Apple is reporting outages affecting several parts of its system, including its App Store, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps and Apple Business. The Federal Aviation Administration is pausing the installation of new routers following a nationwide ground stop on Friday and PR's Joe Hernandez reports maintenance work caused technical disruptions that led to of flight cancellations across the U.S. Federal aviation officials say workers were converting old copper wires to fiber cables when a router made by the company Juniper Networks began flooding the system with information. Now the FAA is pausing the installation of Juniper routers while it continues to investigate what went wrong. That's according to an FAA official who requested anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly. The FAA says it's replaced around 70 percent of the copper wire in its networks so far. It comes as the Trump administration continues to press Congress for billions of dollars in additional funding to modernize the country's air traffic control system. Joe Hernandez, NPR News. President Trump is preparing to travel to China in the morning for a historic trilateral meeting with Presidents Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin of Russia on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Trump has said the war in Ukraine is on the agenda but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky will not be at the summit and says he's concerned about his country's fate being discussed in his absence. Trump has been staying the night in Manila Philippines after attending the ASEAN summit. The US and China are in the midst of an AI race but are also competing on numerous other fronts including in mineral rich Africa. Here's Kate Bartlett in Johannesburg. China is, by far, Africa's biggest trading partner, and now more and more African countries are turning to the Chinese yuan for trade and to pay their debt. Christian Gérôt-Nima is an editor with the China Global South project. He points out several African countries, like Kenya, have already restructured their debt to China. It really just makes sense for many African countries now to starting to trade with China in renminbi instead of trading with China in US dollar. The Trump administration shifting tariff policies have only strengthened the case for African businesses to diversify away from the dollar. Kate Bartlett, NPR News, Johannesburg. Iran fired drones at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain today. Bahrain says it intercepted those drones. Iran recently resumed strikes on neighbors allied with the United States. This is NPR News. The key measure of retail sales barely rose two-tenths of a percent in October compared to September. People spent less on autos and auto parts and really scaled back home improvement purchases. The data does show the impact of Halloween. Spending in the category of stores called miscellaneous rose 4.7 percent compared to September. In the October data also shifts notably comparing this year to October of last year, up nearly 7%. People spent more at restaurants and bars. sales were up nearly 12%, in part thanks to Prime Day and Halloween. And higher gas prices kept driving a surge of spending at gas stations, up nearly 30% from last year. Alina Saluch, NPR News. The administrations repeal to Biden their rule meant to make salaries for federal childcare providers more competitive than Pierre Sequoia Corrillo. The Trump administration published a final rule in the Federal Register on Monday to roll back a Biden-era policy that would have raised educator salaries in the nation's largest federal childcare program, Head Start. The rule was finalized in 2024 and would have gone into effect in 2031. This move is part of a broader push by the administration to deregulate the program. They estimate these changes will result in over $2 billion in cost savings. But Head Start advocates argue that in order to maintain quality services and attract talent to Head Start centers, the program needs to re-evaluate how much it pays its workers. Sequoia Carillo, NPR News. You're listening to NPR News.
